## Current certification course allocation and daily budget

Day 001 · 2026-10-14 · verified curriculum snapshot 13 October 2026. This is a proposed learning allocation, not a learner-ready or completed assignment.

This is the single active certification allocation. It supersedes the previous SAA-first/DVA-C02 exam sequence, generic five-minute review, and conflicting course/budget wording. No extra study block is added. Linked components have 0 additional scheduled minutes. Capstone acceptance outcomes, source history and 150-minute cap stay intact.

**Authoritative combined timebox: 150 minutes maximum.** Capstone focused docs 10m + bounded build 55m + tests/actual evidence 30m =95m; certification theory/source 20m + questions/explanations 10m =30m; DSA 15m; DSM/design reflection 10m.

All embedded historical component/timebox figures below are superseded only for current scheduling by this allocation. Retained component(s) share the same 95-minute capstone envelope; do not charge certification, DSA or DSM twice. The original IDs, dates, scaffold, acceptance cases and completion requirements remain. No extra evening or catch-up work is implied.

INSTRUCTOR_TIMEBOX_CHECK_REQUIRED. Keep the existing capstone acceptance contract; before assigning, prove its supplied scaffold and TODO fit the 95-minute docs/build/test envelope. If not, mark OVER_CAPACITY and propose an explicit in-budget reduction before the learner day; do not compress by assertion, add evening work, silently drop tests, or call the ticket learner-ready.

### Verified Udemy content selected for this day

PENDING_ENTITLEMENT_CHECK: Udemy catalog titles/sections/durations verified 13 October 2026; owned courses, subscription inclusion, playable access and prior attempts are unknown. If unavailable, use the linked official source in the same slot and record ACCESS_PENDING. No purchase or enrollment is authorized.

- [[NEW] Ultimate AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01](https://www.udemy.com/course/aws-ai-practitioner-certified/) · Section 3, **Introduction to AWS & Cloud Computing** · **What is Cloud Computing?** · entire lecture; assigned runtime 7:52. The title and full duration are catalog facts; this date and interval are our proposed mapping.
- [[NEW] Ultimate AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01](https://www.udemy.com/course/aws-ai-practitioner-certified/) · Section 3, **Introduction to AWS & Cloud Computing** · **The Different Types of Cloud Computing** · entire lecture; assigned runtime 3:19. The title and full duration are catalog facts; this date and interval are our proposed mapping.
- [[NEW] Ultimate AWS Certified AI Practitioner AIF-C01](https://www.udemy.com/course/aws-ai-practitioner-certified/) · Section 3, **Introduction to AWS & Cloud Computing** · **Shared Responsibility Model & AWS Acceptable Policy** · entire lecture; assigned runtime 1:36. The title and full duration are catalog facts; this date and interval are our proposed mapping.

Assigned playback total: 12:47 at 1×. Playback is capped at 18m; reserve at least 2m of the 20m theory/source slot for objective review. Any unused playback time goes to source checking or retrieval practice, not another required video.

Optional Cloud Practitioner foundation check within this 30-minute slot: use the listed cloud/shared-responsibility videos, then answer 3 original recall prompts on IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, Regions/AZs and shared responsibility. Record weak concepts. This is a knowledge check, not a Cloud Practitioner exam commitment; foundational gaps replace later theory time rather than adding days. Watching a lecture mentioning policy does not accept any agreement.

### Official objective relevance, not a mastery claim

- [AIF-C01 task 5.1](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/ai-practitioner-01/ai-practitioner-01-domain5.html) · VERIFIED_CURRENT_OBJECTIVE; PROPOSED_LECTURE_RELEVANCE; NOT_MASTERY. These are curriculum-relevance links; keep any existing no-direct-mapping label on today's capstone implementation.

### Practice-question source

- [Introduction to AWS & Cloud Computing - Quiz](https://www.udemy.com/course/aws-ai-practitioner-certified/) · TOPIC_PRACTICE_NOT_FULL_MOCK. Up to 2–3 relevant items; actual per-quiz inventory unknown. Select only verified unused IDs/ordinals from the attempt ledger; repeats are review.

The 15-minute DSA allocation is minimum retention, not a replacement for assigned Java/Top150 outcomes. Relevant Java/DSA implementation and due reviews explicitly remain inside the practical build slice on the days that assign them. Preserve the canonical problem order and history; do not mark attempted as solved or silently remove original learning outcomes.

Log the actual lecture interval completed, exam/version/objective, question source and count, first-attempt score, one explained correction and due date; keep the capstone commit/command/fixture/pass-fail-not-run evidence separate. Do not reproduce proprietary question text.

Reading/watching only. Hands On denotes the instructor demonstration; it does not authorize account creation, credential generation, IAM/security changes, AWS spending, enrollment, purchase or exam booking. Real cloud labs require separately authorized access/budget.

Follow the official AWS Software Development Engineer pathway: optional Cloud Practitioner foundation check; AI Practitioner; Developer Associate; then readiness-gated DevOps Engineer Professional. Generative AI Developer Professional is a deeper extension, not an automatic extra exam. SAA content is selected architecture support only. Professional exams are not promised within this 228-day window.


### Official AWS pathway and version gate

[AWS role-based pathway, current homepage-linked 2026 PDF](https://d1.awsstatic.com/onedam/marketing-channels/website/aws/en_US/certification/approved/pdfs/AWS_certification_paths.pdf). [AWS eligibility policy](https://aws.amazon.com/certification/policies/before-testing/) confirms that these are recommended paths, not mandatory certification prerequisites. The course sequence follows the Software Development Engineer row.

Follow the official AWS Software Development Engineer pathway: optional Cloud Practitioner foundation check; AI Practitioner; Developer Associate; then readiness-gated DevOps Engineer Professional. Generative AI Developer Professional is a deeper extension, not an automatic extra exam. SAA content is selected architecture support only. Professional exams are not promised within this 228-day window.

### Question-pool and repeat control

Candidate training source: [Practice Test #1 - Full-Exam - AWS Certified AI Practitioner](https://www.udemy.com/course/practice-exams-aws-certified-ai-practitioner/). Rotate training Tests 1, 2; reserve Tests 3, 4 unseen for full-readiness simulations. The catalog verified test titles, not the per-test question inventory. Pool alignment: AIF-C01.

Use section quizzes first. Rotate candidate training tests only if the player permits bounded topic practice. Inspect test inventory and the saved attempt ledger first. Record course/test ID, platform question ID or stable test/version/ordinal, objective, first-seen date, attempt count, result and review due date. Count only actually unseen questions as fresh; once the available training pool is exhausted, use logged error review or separately sourced official questions and state the change. Never draw from reserved tests without moving the readiness gate. No question-text copying.

Do not assume unlimited fresh questions or a fixed per-test question count. If the player does not support bounded topic selection, use a relevant section quiz or explicitly labeled error review; do not start a full mock in a 30-minute slot.

## Preserved capstone learning contract

# 2026-10-14 · Daily primary

## Active CoverStory contract · proposed semantic migration

Choose composite Java collection keys for device-local health selections, preserving first-seen order; retrieve exact source excerpts in the linked component.

BLOCKED / NOT_READY_FOR_LEARNER. This is a proposed instructor contract, not installed scaffolding, runnable acceptance proof or learner completion. Instructor must reconcile actual code paths/signatures, pin compatible versions, supply starter TODOs and mutually satisfiable fixtures, repair existing SQL boundary/seeded-map/smoke-501 oracle defects, run setup independent of TODO success, prove a known defect fails and correct behavior passes privately, then rehearse the whole 95-minute task with actual timing. Record command, commit, versions, fixture and actual output. Never expose a completed learner solution. The audited baseline currently exposes Spring /health with scanning limited to capstone.app, and React is in fixture mode. Instructor must deliberately configure the six-module bootstrap, public interfaces and private persistence; add a test rejecting a forbidden cross-module repository import and a dependency cycle. JdbcEventDatabase is only a generic transaction harness and contains no insurance logic.

### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.
Health-first discovery with health/term/motor/ULIP entry links. Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. Catalog editor, Applicant, assigned Support and sandbox simulator are distinct actors.
All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. Explicit final submit after complete fields/disclosures, confirmed corrections, current exact revision/quote/options/terms acceptance and fully reconciled payments produces SUBMISSION_PENDING. Only retained simulated external-dispatch reference evidence can produce SUBMITTED. Policy issuance and active-cover evidence remain separate later states.
Proposed canonical API /api/v1 and noun catalog; no route, package or alias is claimed implemented. Later recovered /api/... routes are documented legacy aliases only pending explicit adapter tests; unversioned /applications, /orders, /quote-validations, /me routes normalize under /api/v1. Historical /api/catalogue/options maps to proposed /api/v1/catalog/options. Historical correlationId maps to requestId in safe errors {code, message, fieldErrors, requestId, retryable}. Old /api/events, /api/pipelines and operator-v1 are historical generic contracts, NOT automatic aliases. Schemas get separate typed adapters and fixtures, never enum renames.
Use trusted actor + operation + resource + key and canonical payload hash. Same key/hash replays stored result; different payload conflicts. A proposed 7-day sandbox response cache does not bound durable resource-effect uniqueness; effect records and reconciliation evidence must survive the applicable retry/retention window. Real legal/provider retention remains a launch gate. UNKNOWN money or dispatch outcomes require same-reference reconciliation before another effect.

### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. Keep audit/backup/key recovery references under reviewed holds; the encryption/key-rotation/deletion plan cannot silently destroy required history. All implementation, prerequisite, encryption, privacy and timebox evidence remains NOT_RUN/BLOCKED.

### Updated protection, revision and recovery boundaries

Preserve ApplicationRevision’s recovered composite key. journey(application_id, application_revision) references application_revision(application_id, revision); no new application-revision UUID is introduced. Local AEAD AAD includes immutable object ID, object revision, payload kind and encryption schema version. Deployment KMS context, if ever authorized, contains non-sensitive constant service/payload-class/version labels only.
Field envelopes do not encrypt every metadata column, foreign key or index. Deployment preparation separately requires authenticated TLS for browser/API and application/database links, encrypted database volumes and backups, key separation, authorized restore and application/proxy/error-log redaction. Local loopback tests prove none of those deployment controls. No configuration/security mutation is authorized here.
An ephemeral in-memory teaching key supports only its declared process lifetime. In-process round-trip, application restart, database restart and restored-backup recovery are separate experiments. Cross-process encrypted recovery is BLOCKED until an approved retained teaching-key mechanism is prepared and verified. A lost key returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE and retains ciphertext; it is never interpreted as empty data or a passing restore. Persist a pending operation/provider reference before any external mock call. If recording a provider result rolls back, retain the prior pending/unknown reference for reconciliation; do not claim a FAILED audit row survived rollback.

### Planned shared frontend foundation

Planned frontend convention: the instructor-supplied SPA shell uses TanStack React Query for server state, shared parameterized UI primitives and compositions, Tailwind design tokens and an Inter/system-ui font stack. This replaces repeated bespoke view blocks while preserving CoverStory’s warm paper surfaces, category accents, accessible controls, responsive spacing and light/dark behavior. Inter is the latest approved open-source font choice; there is no Proxima Nova purchase or licensing blocker. All package versions, setup, components and browser behavior remain unimplemented until the instructor reconciles them with the actual fixture-only frontend.
Query cache is not form or navigation state. Keep unsubmitted input and device-local public selections in their appropriate bounded state. Use typed, versioned query keys containing the relevant public catalog revision or authenticated owner/session generation. A fresh SPA load authenticates, then refetches /api/v1/me/journeys and validates current allowed actions; this is refresh/resume, not an SSR hydration claim. Cancel and clear private queries on logout/account change and ignore late prior-session responses. Do not persist sensitive query data in browser storage. Mutation completion invalidates or updates only the affected owned query/version after authoritative server success; a click, optimistic animation or analytics receipt cannot establish paid/submitted state. The instructor supplies adapters and reusable components; each day retains its single bounded learner seam.

### Frontend provider and build guardrails

The current proposed framework is TanStack React Query v5; verify the actual package version before implementation. Supply one stable QueryClient at the app boundary and domain-owned typed query-key/options factories. Shared primitives do not fetch another module’s data. Stale time, garbage-collection time and retry limits are chosen by data class; authentication and validation failures do not loop. Pass AbortSignal to the actual transport. Refresh and refetch effects never initiate payment, submission or renewal mutations. Do not introduce Next.js, TanStack Start or SSR. Later optional cache-restoration exercises use synthetic public reference data only, with version buster, finite maxAge and suitable gcTime; private cache and queued mutations remain excluded.
Planned shared paths are frontend/src/coverstory/shared/ui/, shared/theme/ and shared/query/. Tailwind semantic tokens centralize color, spacing, radius, focus and typography; finite variant/size/tone props map to complete static utility strings, never dynamic class fragments. The instructor checks the installed Tailwind major before using v4 @theme and verifies production source scanning. Inter/system-ui remains a font token; retain the Inter copyright and SIL Open Font License with later distributed assets. No font download, package install or production build is performed by this draft.

### Existing calendar and timebox

One existing 228-day CAP calendar, 14 October 2026–29 May 2027; this draft changes only Day001–076. Preserve IDs, active dates, roles, board membership, native links, original history and statuses. Each primary150 scheduled minutes; components0 additional minutes. ECOS twelve 15-day windows are source history, not a second schedule.
Original Java/DSA engineering outcomes remain inside the practical seam. Canonical Top Interview 150 order/history and due reviews remain unchanged, with the separate 15-minute minimum retention slot. Do not mark attempted as solved. Ktor is optional same-budget substitution only. AWS lesson/objective/practice/pathway prefix is preserved byte-for-byte; no extra course, account, enrollment or spending is authorized.
For a component, all numbers except scheduled_minutes describe the owning primary envelope and are not additional allocations. Sunday105 practical consists of95 task+10 existing individual evidence, no extra reflection block. Weekday95+30+15+10=150. Sunday95+10+30+15=150.
The two retained contracts below share docs10/build55/tests30=95m: primary docs5/build35/tests20 and component docs5/build20/tests10. Neither has separate scheduled minutes.

### Instructor scaffold and learner TODO

Instructor supplies compatible Java21/Maven/JUnit/PostgreSQL or Python runner, typed DTOs/ports, schema/migrations, deterministic fixtures and failing TODO tests; no learner infrastructure work. For UI targets, supplies the thin React shell from the existing 87 designs, styles, routing, controls and test adapters. Only the declared seam is learner-owned.
Reuse earlier reviewed artifacts through public module interfaces. All new namespace/path/schema mappings are planned and require code-owner reconciliation; do not overwrite prior generic teaching fixtures.
Replace the old event-domain deliverable with this one bounded seam. If combined tests cannot fit95m, mark OVER_CAPACITY and explicitly reduce optional breadth before assigning; do not defer required failure tests or add evening work.
Planned paths (not existing implementation):
- src/main/java/capstone/coverstory/shortlist/api/CAP40Seam.java
- src/test/java/capstone/coverstory/shortlist/CAP40Test.java
- fixtures/coverstory/CAP-40/synthetic-v1.json
- docs/assignments/coverstory/CAP-40.md

List<SelectionKey> uniqueSelections(List<SelectionInput> input); SelectionKey(deviceScope, catalogVersionId). Implement only this bounded seam and its focused cases; do not edit fixture oracle, authorization policy or dependencies to force a pass. No completed implementation is supplied.

### Concrete inputs and outputs

Input is an immutable list of SYNTHETIC device-scoped catalog references; return unique exact pairs in encounter order. Reject null list/elements and blank key parts without mutation. This is local identity, not authentication or permission to read a saved shortlist.

### Acceptance cases · expected, NOT_RUN

- CAP-40-CS-01: Input: [(device-A, health-A-v1), (device-A, health-B-v1), (device-A, health-A-v1)]. Expected: A-v1, B-v1 in that order; original list unchanged.
- CAP-40-CS-02: Input: []. Expected: [].
- CAP-40-CS-03: Input: same version in device-A and device-B. Expected: Two independent keys.
- CAP-40-CS-04: Input: blank catalogVersionId. Expected: IllegalArgumentException and no partial result.

### Included retained component [CAP-41](https://dwait-to-adwait.youtrack.cloud/issue/CAP-41) · zero additional minutes

No earlier CAP prerequisite; instructor readiness still required.

Primary and linked component share one evidence sheet: combined maximum 5 minutes, 3 changed facts, 6 nodes or 10 messages for the whole day. Use the instructor-supplied UML/data-flow template and today’s existing test/receipt in docs/evidence/coverstory/CAP-40/result.json. Annotate the supplied SelectionKey(deviceScope, catalogVersionId) → membership check → ordered output sketch. Record only these changed facts: Identity includes both key components.; First encounter determines output position..

### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.
Health-first discovery with health/term/motor/ULIP entry links. Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. Catalog editor, Applicant, assigned Support and sandbox simulator are distinct actors.
All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. Explicit final submit after complete fields/disclosures, confirmed corrections, current exact revision/quote/options/terms acceptance and fully reconciled payments produces SUBMISSION_PENDING. Only retained simulated external-dispatch reference evidence can produce SUBMITTED. Policy issuance and active-cover evidence remain separate later states.
Proposed canonical API /api/v1 and noun catalog; no route, package or alias is claimed implemented. Later recovered /api/... routes are documented legacy aliases only pending explicit adapter tests; unversioned /applications, /orders, /quote-validations, /me routes normalize under /api/v1. Historical /api/catalogue/options maps to proposed /api/v1/catalog/options. Historical correlationId maps to requestId in safe errors {code, message, fieldErrors, requestId, retryable}. Old /api/events, /api/pipelines and operator-v1 are historical generic contracts, NOT automatic aliases. Schemas get separate typed adapters and fixtures, never enum renames.
Use trusted actor + operation + resource + key and canonical payload hash. Same key/hash replays stored result; different payload conflicts. A proposed 7-day sandbox response cache does not bound durable resource-effect uniqueness; effect records and reconciliation evidence must survive the applicable retry/retention window. Real legal/provider retention remains a launch gate. UNKNOWN money or dispatch outcomes require same-reference reconciliation before another effect.

### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. Keep audit/backup/key recovery references under reviewed holds; the encryption/key-rotation/deletion plan cannot silently destroy required history. All implementation, prerequisite, encryption, privacy and timebox evidence remains NOT_RUN/BLOCKED.

### Updated protection, revision and recovery boundaries

Preserve ApplicationRevision’s recovered composite key. journey(application_id, application_revision) references application_revision(application_id, revision); no new application-revision UUID is introduced. Local AEAD AAD includes immutable object ID, object revision, payload kind and encryption schema version. Deployment KMS context, if ever authorized, contains non-sensitive constant service/payload-class/version labels only.
Field envelopes do not encrypt every metadata column, foreign key or index. Deployment preparation separately requires authenticated TLS for browser/API and application/database links, encrypted database volumes and backups, key separation, authorized restore and application/proxy/error-log redaction. Local loopback tests prove none of those deployment controls. No configuration/security mutation is authorized here.
An ephemeral in-memory teaching key supports only its declared process lifetime. In-process round-trip, application restart, database restart and restored-backup recovery are separate experiments. Cross-process encrypted recovery is BLOCKED until an approved retained teaching-key mechanism is prepared and verified. A lost key returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE and retains ciphertext; it is never interpreted as empty data or a passing restore. Persist a pending operation/provider reference before any external mock call. If recording a provider result rolls back, retain the prior pending/unknown reference for reconciliation; do not claim a FAILED audit row survived rollback.

### Planned shared frontend foundation

Planned frontend convention: the instructor-supplied SPA shell uses TanStack React Query for server state, shared parameterized UI primitives and compositions, Tailwind design tokens and an Inter/system-ui font stack. This replaces repeated bespoke view blocks while preserving CoverStory’s warm paper surfaces, category accents, accessible controls, responsive spacing and light/dark behavior. Inter is the latest approved open-source font choice; there is no Proxima Nova purchase or licensing blocker. All package versions, setup, components and browser behavior remain unimplemented until the instructor reconciles them with the actual fixture-only frontend.
Query cache is not form or navigation state. Keep unsubmitted input and device-local public selections in their appropriate bounded state. Use typed, versioned query keys containing the relevant public catalog revision or authenticated owner/session generation. A fresh SPA load authenticates, then refetches /api/v1/me/journeys and validates current allowed actions; this is refresh/resume, not an SSR hydration claim. Cancel and clear private queries on logout/account change and ignore late prior-session responses. Do not persist sensitive query data in browser storage. Mutation completion invalidates or updates only the affected owned query/version after authoritative server success; a click, optimistic animation or analytics receipt cannot establish paid/submitted state. The instructor supplies adapters and reusable components; each day retains its single bounded learner seam.

No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.
Health-first discovery with health/term/motor/ULIP entry links. Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. Catalog editor, Applicant, assigned Support and sandbox simulator are distinct actors.
All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. Explicit final submit after complete fields/disclosures, confirmed corrections, current exact revision/quote/options/terms acceptance and fully reconciled payments produces SUBMISSION_PENDING. Only retained simulated external-dispatch reference evidence can produce SUBMITTED. Policy issuance and active-cover evidence remain separate later states.
Proposed canonical API /api/v1 and noun catalog; no route, package or alias is claimed implemented. Later recovered /api/... routes are documented legacy aliases only pending explicit adapter tests; unversioned /applications, /orders, /quote-validations, /me routes normalize under /api/v1. A proposed 7-day sandbox response cache does not bound durable resource-effect uniqueness; effect records and reconciliation evidence must survive the applicable retry/retention window. Real legal/provider retention remains a launch gate. UNKNOWN money or dispatch outcomes require same-reference reconciliation before another effect.

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. ### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.

Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. ### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. Keep audit/backup/key recovery references under reviewed holds; the encryption/key-rotation/deletion plan cannot silently destroy required history. All implementation, prerequisite, encryption, privacy and timebox evidence remains NOT_RUN/BLOCKED.

Preserve ApplicationRevision’s recovered composite key. journey(application_id, application_revision) references application_revision(application_id, revision); no new application-revision UUID is introduced. Field envelopes do not encrypt every metadata column, foreign key or index. An ephemeral in-memory teaching key supports only its declared process lifetime. In-process round-trip, application restart, database restart and restored-backup recovery are separate experiments. A lost key returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE and retains ciphertext; it is never interpreted as empty data or a passing restore. Persist a pending operation/provider reference before any external mock call. ## Preserved capstone learning contract

# 2026-10-18 · Linked component of CAP-48

## Active CoverStory contract · proposed semantic migration

Distinguish missing, wrong-source and wrong-version evidence instead of inflating answer success.

BLOCKED / NOT_READY_FOR_LEARNER. This is a proposed instructor contract, not installed scaffolding, runnable acceptance proof or learner completion. Instructor must reconcile actual code paths/signatures, pin compatible versions, supply starter TODOs and mutually satisfiable fixtures, repair existing SQL boundary/seeded-map/smoke-501 oracle defects, run setup independent of TODO success, prove a known defect fails and correct behavior passes privately, then rehearse the whole 95-minute task with actual timing. Record command, commit, versions, fixture and actual output. Never expose a completed learner solution. The audited baseline currently exposes Spring /health with scanning limited to capstone.app, and React is in fixture mode. Instructor must deliberately configure the six-module bootstrap, public interfaces and private persistence; add a test rejecting a forbidden cross-module repository import and a dependency cycle. JdbcEventDatabase is only a generic transaction harness and contains no insurance logic.

### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.
Health-first discovery with health/term/motor/ULIP entry links. Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. Catalog editor, Applicant, assigned Support and sandbox simulator are distinct actors.
All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. Explicit final submit after complete fields/disclosures, confirmed corrections, current exact revision/quote/options/terms acceptance and fully reconciled payments produces SUBMISSION_PENDING. Only retained simulated external-dispatch reference evidence can produce SUBMITTED. Policy issuance and active-cover evidence remain separate later states.
Proposed canonical API /api/v1 and noun catalog; no route, package or alias is claimed implemented. Later recovered /api/... routes are documented legacy aliases only pending explicit adapter tests; unversioned /applications, /orders, /quote-validations, /me routes normalize under /api/v1. Historical /api/catalogue/options maps to proposed /api/v1/catalog/options. Historical correlationId maps to requestId in safe errors {code, message, fieldErrors, requestId, retryable}. Old /api/events, /api/pipelines and operator-v1 are historical generic contracts, NOT automatic aliases. Schemas get separate typed adapters and fixtures, never enum renames.
Use trusted actor + operation + resource + key and canonical payload hash. Same key/hash replays stored result; different payload conflicts. A proposed 7-day sandbox response cache does not bound durable resource-effect uniqueness; effect records and reconciliation evidence must survive the applicable retry/retention window. Real legal/provider retention remains a launch gate. UNKNOWN money or dispatch outcomes require same-reference reconciliation before another effect.

### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. Keep audit/backup/key recovery references under reviewed holds; the encryption/key-rotation/deletion plan cannot silently destroy required history. All implementation, prerequisite, encryption, privacy and timebox evidence remains NOT_RUN/BLOCKED.

The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. ## Active CoverStory contract · proposed semantic migration

Map domain decisions into a real Spring request-binding seam while the instructor supplies the thin public catalog reader.

BLOCKED / NOT_READY_FOR_LEARNER. This is a proposed instructor contract, not installed scaffolding, runnable acceptance proof or learner completion. Instructor must reconcile actual code paths/signatures, pin compatible versions, supply starter TODOs and mutually satisfiable fixtures, repair existing SQL boundary/seeded-map/smoke-501 oracle defects, run setup independent of TODO success, prove a known defect fails and correct behavior passes privately, then rehearse the whole 95-minute task with actual timing. Record command, commit, versions, fixture and actual output. Never expose a completed learner solution. The audited baseline currently exposes Spring /health with scanning limited to capstone.app, and React is in fixture mode. Instructor must deliberately configure the six-module bootstrap, public interfaces and private persistence; add a test rejecting a forbidden cross-module repository import and a dependency cycle. JdbcEventDatabase is only a generic transaction harness and contains no insurance logic.

### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.
Health-first discovery with health/term/motor/ULIP entry links. Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. Catalog editor, Applicant, assigned Support and sandbox simulator are distinct actors.
All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. Explicit final submit after complete fields/disclosures, confirmed corrections, current exact revision/quote/options/terms acceptance and fully reconciled payments produces SUBMISSION_PENDING. Only retained simulated external-dispatch reference evidence can produce SUBMITTED. Policy issuance and active-cover evidence remain separate later states.
Proposed canonical API /api/v1 and noun catalog; no route, package or alias is claimed implemented. Later recovered /api/... routes are documented legacy aliases only pending explicit adapter tests; unversioned /applications, /orders, /quote-validations, /me routes normalize under /api/v1. Historical /api/catalogue/options maps to proposed /api/v1/catalog/options. Historical correlationId maps to requestId in safe errors {code, message, fieldErrors, requestId, retryable}. Old /api/events, /api/pipelines and operator-v1 are historical generic contracts, NOT automatic aliases. Schemas get separate typed adapters and fixtures, never enum renames.
Use trusted actor + operation + resource + key and canonical payload hash. Same key/hash replays stored result; different payload conflicts. A proposed 7-day sandbox response cache does not bound durable resource-effect uniqueness; effect records and reconciliation evidence must survive the applicable retry/retention window. Real legal/provider retention remains a launch gate. UNKNOWN money or dispatch outcomes require same-reference reconciliation before another effect.

### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. Keep audit/backup/key recovery references under reviewed holds; the encryption/key-rotation/deletion plan cannot silently destroy required history. All implementation, prerequisite, encryption, privacy and timebox evidence remains NOT_RUN/BLOCKED.

### Updated protection, revision and recovery boundaries

Preserve ApplicationRevision’s recovered composite key. journey(application_id, application_revision) references application_revision(application_id, revision); no new application-revision UUID is introduced. Local AEAD AAD includes immutable object ID, object revision, payload kind and encryption schema version. Deployment KMS context, if ever authorized, contains non-sensitive constant service/payload-class/version labels only.
Field envelopes do not encrypt every metadata column, foreign key or index. Deployment preparation separately requires authenticated TLS for browser/API and application/database links, encrypted database volumes and backups, key separation, authorized restore and application/proxy/error-log redaction. Local loopback tests prove none of those deployment controls. No configuration/security mutation is authorized here.
An ephemeral in-memory teaching key supports only its declared process lifetime. In-process round-trip, application restart, database restart and restored-backup recovery are separate experiments. Cross-process encrypted recovery is BLOCKED until an approved retained teaching-key mechanism is prepared and verified. A lost key returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE and retains ciphertext; it is never interpreted as empty data or a passing restore. Persist a pending operation/provider reference before any external mock call. If recording a provider result rolls back, retain the prior pending/unknown reference for reconciliation; do not claim a FAILED audit row survived rollback.

### Planned shared frontend foundation

Planned frontend convention: the instructor-supplied SPA shell uses TanStack React Query for server state, shared parameterized UI primitives and compositions, Tailwind design tokens and an Inter/system-ui font stack. This replaces repeated bespoke view blocks while preserving CoverStory’s warm paper surfaces, category accents, accessible controls, responsive spacing and light/dark behavior. Inter is the latest approved open-source font choice; there is no Proxima Nova purchase or licensing blocker. All package versions, setup, components and browser behavior remain unimplemented until the instructor reconciles them with the actual fixture-only frontend.
Query cache is not form or navigation state. Keep unsubmitted input and device-local public selections in their appropriate bounded state. Use typed, versioned query keys containing the relevant public catalog revision or authenticated owner/session generation. A fresh SPA load authenticates, then refetches /api/v1/me/journeys and validates current allowed actions; this is refresh/resume, not an SSR hydration claim. Cancel and clear private queries on logout/account change and ignore late prior-session responses. Do not persist sensitive query data in browser storage. Mutation completion invalidates or updates only the affected owned query/version after authoritative server success; a click, optimistic animation or analytics receipt cannot establish paid/submitted state. The instructor supplies adapters and reusable components; each day retains its single bounded learner seam.

### Frontend provider and build guardrails

The current proposed framework is TanStack React Query v5; verify the actual package version before implementation. Supply one stable QueryClient at the app boundary and domain-owned typed query-key/options factories. Shared primitives do not fetch another module’s data. Stale time, garbage-collection time and retry limits are chosen by data class; authentication and validation failures do not loop. Pass AbortSignal to the actual transport. Refresh and refetch effects never initiate payment, submission or renewal mutations. Do not introduce Next.js, TanStack Start or SSR. Later optional cache-restoration exercises use synthetic public reference data only, with version buster, finite maxAge and suitable gcTime; private cache and queued mutations remain excluded.
Planned shared paths are frontend/src/coverstory/shared/ui/, shared/theme/ and shared/query/. Tailwind semantic tokens centralize color, spacing, radius, focus and typography; finite variant/size/tone props map to complete static utility strings, never dynamic class fragments. The instructor checks the installed Tailwind major before using v4 @theme and verifies production source scanning. Inter/system-ui remains a font token; retain the Inter copyright and SIL Open Font License with later distributed assets. No font download, package install or production build is performed by this draft.

### Existing calendar and timebox

One existing 228-day CAP calendar, 14 October 2026–29 May 2027; this draft changes only Day001–076. Preserve IDs, active dates, roles, board membership, native links, original history and statuses. Each primary150 scheduled minutes; components0 additional minutes. ECOS twelve 15-day windows are source history, not a second schedule.

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.

### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.

Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. An ephemeral in-memory teaching key supports only its declared process lifetime. In-process round-trip, application restart, database restart and restored-backup recovery are separate experiments. Cross-process encrypted recovery is BLOCKED until an approved retained teaching-key mechanism is prepared and verified. A lost key returns KEY_UNAVAILABLE and retains ciphertext; it is never interpreted as empty data or a passing restore. Persist a pending operation/provider reference before any external mock call. Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. ### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.

Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. ### Fixed scope, architecture and privacy

Proposed React → Spring API → owning Catalog/Shortlist/Application/Payments/Policy/Support public module interface → one PostgreSQL. No cross-module repository access. No runtime broker, Redis cache or second database. Additional technology requires a product need/measured bottleneck, alternatives, failure/cost analysis and linked ADR.

Anonymous browse, compare 1–3 unique same-category and matching-scenario versions, and device-local save/export need no phone, OTP or marketing gate. Keep Unknown as Unknown, critical restrictions expanded, source version/date/evidence label visible. Login is required only for owned objects and mock purchase. Catalog editor, Applicant, assigned Support and sandbox simulator are distinct actors.
All new money uses currency INR and integer minor units. SYNTHETIC fixture quotes exercise contracts only. Captured illustrations, base tariffs and historical rates are SOURCE_EVIDENCE, not accepted payable quotes. Unknown tax/total or unsupported scenario blocks payable review. Every changed amount, terms, quote/configuration or revision requires explicit review/acceptance, including changes at or below 100 paise. The >100-paise threshold adds escalation, never permits silent acceptance.
Mock Juspay and simulated insurer only; no real PII, payments, refunds, policy sales, cloud resources or insurer dispatch. Payment confirmation unlocks one owned ONBOARDING application; it does not submit a proposal or create active cover. Explicit final submit after complete fields/disclosures, confirmed corrections, current exact revision/quote/options/terms acceptance and fully reconciled payments produces SUBMISSION_PENDING. Only retained simulated external-dispatch reference evidence can produce SUBMITTED. Policy issuance and active-cover evidence remain separate later states.
Proposed canonical API /api/v1 and noun catalog; no route, package or alias is claimed implemented. Later recovered /api/... routes are documented legacy aliases only pending explicit adapter tests; unversioned /applications, /orders, /quote-validations, /me routes normalize under /api/v1. Historical /api/catalogue/options maps to proposed /api/v1/catalog/options. Historical correlationId maps to requestId in safe errors {code, message, fieldErrors, requestId, retryable}. Old /api/events, /api/pipelines and operator-v1 are historical generic contracts, NOT automatic aliases. Schemas get separate typed adapters and fixtures, never enum renames.
Use trusted actor + operation + resource + key and canonical payload hash. Same key/hash replays stored result; different payload conflicts. A proposed 7-day sandbox response cache does not bound durable resource-effect uniqueness; effect records and reconciliation evidence must survive the applicable retry/retention window. Real legal/provider retention remains a launch gate. UNKNOWN money or dispatch outcomes require same-reference reconciliation before another effect.

### Proposed journey, audit, analytics and encryption foundations

New user-required foundations are proposed instructor scaffolds, not implemented integrations. Anonymous comparison and device-local save remain open; private journey resume requires an authenticated owner. journey.id is a UUID identifier, never an access credential. Journey stores a server-maintained navigation projection and references exact owned domain records, including ApplicationRevision; it does not duplicate plaintext or encrypted application answers. GET /api/v1/me/journeys returns minimal owner-bound homepage summaries with limit 1–50 and a safe cursor. Browser-supplied steps never establish paid, submitted or issued state.
A validated domain transition, required transaction_audit_event, journey projection update and journey_step_event commit atomically in one PostgreSQL unit of work through public module interfaces. Audit refers to existing orders, attempts, journal effects, adjustments and submission records; it is not a second money ledger. Keep initiated, pending, failed, unknown, reconciled and succeeded observations append-only, with operation/provider references and server-derived integer amounts where applicable. Corrections append; they never erase an earlier observation. No raw provider payload, form values, credentials or free-text exception is copied into audit.
Consumer payloads reside in protected_payload_envelope referenced by their owning domain revision. The instructor must supply and verify a maintained authenticated-encryption adapter before the first private write. Proposed AES-256-GCM uses a 12-byte nonce, 128-bit tag, separate wrapped DEK and KEK reference, unique nonce per encryption under a key, and object/revision/payload-kind/schema-version AAD. Authorization occurs before decrypt. Malformed/tampered envelope, wrong object binding or missing key fails closed with zero plaintext fallback. Keys never enter the repository, browser, database as plaintext, logs or telemetry. Fixed keys/nonces are isolated test-vector fixtures only; no real KMS/key/grant creation is authorized.
PAGE_VIEW and CONTROL_CLICK analytics are separate best-effort observations. POST /api/v1/analytics/events accepts one event or at most 10 events within 8 KiB of UTF-8 JSON. Use versioned page/step/target allowlists and no arbitrary properties, form values, health answers, amounts, contact data, secrets, raw URLs/queries/referrers or DOM text. Validate ownership before linking a journey. Client time/order is untrusted; store server_received_at separately and never use analytics to advance journey or financial state. Policy-disallowed clients emit nothing; defensive arrivals receive DISCARDED_BY_POLICY without payload persistence. 202 receipts mean RECEIVED, DUPLICATE or DISCARDED_BY_POLICY only; changed payload under the same event UUID is 409 EVENT_ID_CONFLICT. Invalid 400, oversized 413 and rate-limited 429 are safe. Browser queue maximum 20 and retries maximum 3 may drop telemetry; checkout, save and resume remain independent. No third-party analytics destination is introduced.
Retention windows remain configurable synthetic teaching values, not legal policy. Keep audit/backup/key recovery references under reviewed holds; the encryption/key-rotation/deletion plan cannot silently destroy required history. All implementation, prerequisite, encryption, privacy and timebox evidence remains NOT_RUN/BLOCKED.
